title: Leadership by Quality – An executive action guide to achieving enduring excellence and social responsibility
desc: There is much discussion about Quality 4.0 and Social Responsibility these days. How should they influence a quality management system? If you are in a position to advise your organization’s leader what would you tell them needs to be accomplished? In this presentation Dr. Watson will expand upon his series of 18 webinars as delivered to the ASQ Quality Management Division since the pandemic began in February 2020. These monthly webinars probed the fundamental modern interpretation of the concept of “Managing for Quality” based on the combined ideas of Juran, Deming, and Ishikawa and interpreted them in the light of the disrupting turbulence that is arising from the increasing application of digital technologies as they creep in to our daily personal and working lives. In this presentation Dr. Watson will put himself in your place and go through a thinking process and conversation that almost every quality professional will need to have in the coming years. This will give you an opportunity to consider: how will you advise your own management team to cope with the turmoil that is coming to technology and humanity as a result of this transformation?

title: Drug Additions: Current State and Structural Changes that can Help
desc: This talk will address the current state of drug addiction in this region and some structural changes that have occurred in recent years that have helped with the treatment of drug addiction. It will also address some barriers to effective treatments and structural changes that might help overcome these barriers.

title: Expectations for corrective action responses from audit findings
desc:
Expectations for corrective action responses from IATF/ISO/AS audit findings.
What is expected from corrective actions related to QMS audits?
Common pitfalls when responding to audit findings.
Risks associated with poor corrective action responses.

title: Remote Leadership: Role Model Practices
desc: The workplace isn’t like it used to be. What do your team members need from you? How do you keep them engaged? How do you create a successful remote workplace culture? How do I keep them interested even during meetings? It was easier when we were face-to-face.

title: Integration of a Clinical Pharmacist into Clinical Practice and a Quality Improvement Team
desc:
Objectives:
1) Describe the difference in education and training for a clinical pharmacist
2) Review a method to identify high risk patients for a clinical pharmacist
3) Discuss the evolution of clinical pharmacist interventions in a process that improves quality measures

title: What is Statistical Process Control?
desc: Statistical Process Control (SPC) is a powerful methodology that helps users understand and improve their processes. This talk will cover some basic tools of SPC and how they can be applied to both manufacturing and non-manufacturing spaces. Topics will include evaluating process variation, assessing process performance relative to expected behavior and customer requirements, and directing process improvement efforts.

title: Lean for Service
desc: Lean is getting rid of all possible non-value adding activities (all waste). Learn the basics of Lean and the best practices of applying Lean to service type of businesses.

title: SPC for Autocorrelated Data Using Automated Time Series Forecasting
desc:
Review the problem of Statistical Process Control (SPC) for autocorrelated data.
Review the use of Simple Exponential Smoothing/Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) to implement SPC for autocorrelated data.
Become familiar with recent developments in time series forecasting that automate advanced model selection and estimation.
Learn how to easily apply these methods to Statistical Process Control charts for autocorrelated data.
